translated_text: Ame Zabis helps Tüchlacker 10. 1.3.5 I want to help you so much and I don't know how. Sometimes it's maddening that all that's left is the feeling of belonging. But nothing else. That makes me feel like I was perhaps even drained by the powerlessness, somewhat indifferent. But I know that these are just my current moods, and I hope that some really good news from you and here will soon give me more options. Say my best regards and wish your dear mother a speedy recovery. In Prague, I was very pleased to see that my parents have settled in very well. I would love to go there too; but it was very, very nice and I can't stay at least until I can find something better there. You know how difficult that is these days, my dear. By the way, my parents are moving into a very nice apartment today, quite similar to the one on Maximilianstrasse. Just a little smaller. Mom is very happy about it; they absolutely want me to come to them right away! But this is—besides the desire itself—unreasonable on my part and completely out of the question. I want to earn some money first. I'll be leaving in February and will be in Mannheim on the 23rd, here on January 20th, and in Frankfurt from around the 29th. From then on, I'll have to leave it up to you, or rather, let's leave it to fate, whether there's still a chance for us to meet in January or not. Yes, write to us about it soon, my dear. Do you hope, do you believe, for maybe... The more I delve into it, the greater my hopes become that I—that's what's left, even if it's an illusion. Write again soon, your Bob 726.
